The only time _relatedTarget_ seems to actually impact the event path is step 6.9.7: > Otherwise, if _parent_ is _relatedTarget_, then set _parent_ to null. This seems to have been added in https://github.com/whatwg/dom/commit/afac5044c18fa871837b0a86d21f338b29f7a292, with the commit message: > Shadow: do not dispatch an event when target is relatedTarget > > For example, when a mouse pointer moves from an element in a shadow tree to its shadow host, a mouseover event should not be dispatched on the shadow host. > @keithamus The spec already retargets the `source` getter:
> 
> https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-commandevent-source
> 
> > The source getter steps are to return the result of [retargeting](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#retarget) [source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-commandevent-source) against [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [currentTarget](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-currenttarget).

Perhaps it's a separate issue, but there needs to be additional work to solve issues of retargeting when `currentTarget` is `null`:

```
data:text/html,<div id=a><template shadowrootmode=open><button command=show-modal>Click</template><dialog id=p><script>a.shadowRoot.querySelector('button').commandForElement = p;</script><script>p.addEventListener('command', async e => new Promise(setTimeout).then(()=>console.log(e.source)))</script>
```
```html
<div id=a>
<template shadowrootmode=open><button command=show-modal>Click</template>
<dialog id=p>
<script>a.shadowRoot.querySelector('button').commandForElement = p;</script>
<script>
p.addEventListener('command', async e =>
  new Promise(setTimeout).then(()=>console.log(e.source)))
</script>
```

I think issues like this are where the preference for `.source` to retarget like `.relatedTarget` are coming from. This remains an issue regardless of `composed` being true or false, but we should settle on a direction for what we're doing with `.source`. Perhaps this doesn't _block_ making command events non composed but it is why I left my comment.
I found the same issue that keith mentioned, here is a chromium patch that addresses it. I can make a spec PR for it soon: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/6526266
Could you explain what the difference is with that and why the existing retarget doesn't work? A spec pr will obviously help but a plain English explanation would help me understand a bit easier?

The current getter retargets against currentTarget if currentTarget is present, and otherwise just returns the original element. After event dispatch, currentTarget becomes null, so it just returns the original element. If the original element is a node inside a shadow root which shouldn't be leaked, then listening to the event outside of the shadow root will return the correctly retargeted thing during event dispatch, but if you save the event and then look at it again after event dispatch is complete, it will incorrectly return the non-retargeted element which can leak nodes inside the shadow root.
